claimsToVerify: Viking-age Scandinavian longhouses routinely housed livestock and people under the same roof for winter heat.
Stockfish, cured dairy (like skyr), and flatbreads were dietary staples during winter.
Warp-weighted looms and textile production were major indoor winter activities in Norse households.
